title: Ninada: Sub-Clause Split-Graph VITS Streaming and Capability-Routed 24 kHz Speech Synthesis Across Twelve Scripts
abstract: arXiv:2611.10035v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: End-to-end VITS text-to-speech models synthesize natural speech in a single forward pass, yet standard ONNX exports execute monolithically over an entire clause, delaying Time-To-First-Audio (TTFA) to several seconds and spiking activation memory. Client-side deployment across Indic scripts faces four further bottlenecks: 138.8 MB float32 checkpoints per language strain browser caches, mobile WebGPU stalls for 6-14 s compiling convolution shaders while still running slower than real time ($1.44\times$ RTF), small WebAssembly pthread pools stall at barriers on big-LITTLE mobile CPUs, and mobile Web Audio pipelines drop frames or mute output under AudioWorklet contention and iOS WKWebView rules.   We present Ninada, an open-source 24 kHz TTS system covering English, Classical Sanskrit, and ten Indian languages (sa, en, hi, kn, mr, bn, ta, te, ml, gu, pa, or) across a capability-routed 48-checkpoint fleet: 24 studio HiFi-GAN v1 speciali

translated_title: Ninada：子句级拆分图 VITS 流式合成与能力路由的 24 kHz 跨十二种文字语音合成
translated_abstract: 端到端 VITS 文本转语音模型能够在单次前向传播中合成自然语音，然而标准的 ONNX 导出是以单体方式对整个子句执行的，这会使首音频时间（TTFA）延迟到数秒，并导致激活内存激增。跨印度语系文字的客户端部署还面临四个额外瓶颈：每种语言 138.8 MB 的 float32 检查点使浏览器缓存不堪重负；移动端 WebGPU 在编译卷积着色器时停顿 6-14 秒，且运行速度仍慢于实时（1.44× RTF）；小型 WebAssembly 线程池在 big·LITTLE 移动 CPU 的同步屏障处停滞；移动端 Web Audio 管线在 AudioWorklet 竞争和 iOS WKWebView 规则限制下出现丢帧或静音输出。我们提出了 Ninada，一个开源的 24 kHz 语音合成系统，覆盖英语、古典梵语和十种印度语言（sa、en、hi、kn、mr、bn、ta、te、ml、gu、pa、or），通过能力路由的 48 个检查点舰队实现：其中 24 个为录音室级 HiFi-GAN v1 专用……（原文摘要至此被截断）
tldr: Ninada 是一个开源 24 kHz 多语言语音合成系统，通过子句级拆分图 VITS 流式推理、能力路由的 48 检查点舰队以及针对浏览器与移动端的一系列优化，解决了英语、梵语及十种印度语言共十二种文字在客户端部署中首音频延迟、模型体积、WebGPU 编译停顿、线程池阻塞和音频管线丢帧等瓶颈。
en_tdlr: Ninada is an open-source 24 kHz TTS system that combines sub-clause split-graph VITS streaming with a capability-routed 48-checkpoint fleet to overcome TTFA latency, memory, and browser/mobile deployment bottlenecks for client-side speech synthesis across twelve scripts, including English, Classical Sanskrit, and ten Indian languages.
